office_does: The County Auditor runs elections and voter registration, records property documents, issues marriage and vehicle licenses, and keeps the county's financial records and reports.
race_blurb: Open seat after Greg Kimsey's 28 years in office. Mitchell Kelly, a 10-year manager inside the office whom Kimsey informally supports, faces former County Council chair Eileen Quiring O'Brien, who pledges a Day-1 outside audit of the office and its voter rolls. The two finished within half a point of each other in the primary.

candidates.summary: Former Clark County Council chair and Oregon legislator running as an outside reformer of the auditor's office, with an independent audit of finances, elections and voter rolls as her central pledge.
highlights: Pledges a complete independent third-party audit of the office on her first day, including voter rolls, with results published [S9]
Promises a search to eliminate "waste, fraud and abuse" of taxpayer resources [S1]
Says eligibility should be checked proactively against databases rather than relying on self-attestation [S10]
Only primary candidate who said she would support limits on mail-in voting, though she says vote-by-mail is too popular to end now [S7]
Endorsed by the Clark County Republican Party [S10]

spending.basis: Repeatedly centers her campaign on an outside audit of the office's entire finances and a search for waste, fraud and abuse.

experience.basis: Long elected record (Oregon Legislature, county council chair), but she runs as the 'fresh eyes' change candidate against an inside successor.

candidates.summary: Ten-year Clark County Auditor's Office finance manager and former assistant state auditor, running as the continuity candidate with the outgoing auditor's informal support.
highlights: Controller and then reporting and analysis manager in the auditor's office for 10 years; former assistant state auditor [S1]
Says the auditor's role "is not political — it is procedural" [S3]
Says federal and state law limit voter-roll removals and wants to counter misinformation by explaining each step of the election process [S12]
Recommended by The Columbian's editorial board; endorsed by building-trades and labor councils and Vancouver firefighters [S11][S2]

experience.basis: A decade inside the office and Kimsey's informal support, running on continuity, but never elected to any office.
